**No — the papers do not describe cobalt-free cathodes as having flat voltage profiles in general.** It depends on the cathode family, and for the main families discussed the profiles are either sloping or the papers do not describe their shape.

**Disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes: sloping**
- The review explicitly lists "sloping voltage profiles resulting from the extent of TM cation disorder" as a technical challenge for DRX cathodes (aenm-2022, p. 9).
- They operate at moderate voltages (2.5–3.5 V vs Li/Li⁺) (aenm-2022, p. 9).

**Ni-rich layered cobalt-free cathodes (e.g., NFA, LiNiₓFeᵧAl_zO₂): solid-solution behavior, not a single flat plateau**
- GITT profiles showed "solid solution behavior," consistent with the voltammetry (adma-2020, p. 8).
- Cyclic voltammetry shows three redox couples at about 3.75, 4.0 and 4.3 V. These correspond to the hexagonal-1 ↔ monoclinic, monoclinic ↔ hexagonal-2 and hexagonal-2 ↔ hexagonal-3 transitions (adma-2020, p. 8).
- These transitions are said to mirror those of conventional cobalt-containing NCM and NCA materials (adma-2020, p. 6).
- Charge/discharge was run over 3–4.5 V (adma-2020, p. 8). Other Co-free Ni-rich cathodes (NMM, NMT, NMA) were likewise cycled over 2.8–4.5 V (aenm-2022, p. 8). Neither paper calls these profiles flat.

**Olivine and spinel cathodes (LiFePO₄, LiMn₂O₄, LiNi₀.₅Mn₁.₅O₄)**
- The review gives a characteristic operating voltage for each but never describes the profile shape:
  - LFP: about 3.4 V via the Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ couple (aenm-2022, p. 9).
  - LNMO: about 4.7 V (aenm-2022, p. 9).
- So the documents do not state whether these profiles are flat.

**Bottom line:** Of the cobalt-free systems covered, DRX cathodes are explicitly described as sloping. Ni-rich layered Co-free cathodes show solid-solution behavior with several phase-transition redox features, as NCM/NCA do. The papers do not claim a flat voltage profile for any cobalt-free class.
